sound: All 13 watchlists audit items checked as fixed in code: given company only, one-word company held, partial for names that cannot be screened, transliteration, failed lists, cut searches, name variants, stale copies, ended-EBRD wording, FRB recent-file check, associates, kin text. The LEIE monthly file was parsed live: 84k rows in 0.25s, about 0.2s to screen, 3.9 MB stored, under the 6 MB cap. Live EU/UK/US lists parse and screen correctly (Cyrillic too). The alias path, retractions (live), FRB and academicMore grades were checked. No privacy leak was found in the list text.

findings.title: EU data-protection fines: real fines against Klarna, Avast and Deliveroo are dropped and the report says 'found no fine'
findings.evidence: Fed the live tracker page (3,432 cases) through gdprFinesConnector.run. For Klarna, Deliveroo and Avast the result was no findings plus the note 'found no fine against it'. The tracker lists 'Klarna Bank AB' (EUR 720k), 'Deliveroo Italy s.r.l.' (EUR 2.5M) and 'Avast Software s.r.o.' (EUR 13.9M).
findings.scenario: The company is typed as Klarna, Avast or Deliveroo. matchCase calls exposure.matchOrgName. Its LEGAL set has no EU forms (uab, sro, ou, kft, doo...), and it treats words such as Bank, Software or Italy as neither padding nor sector words, so it returns null for every party. No 'possible' finding is kept either. The person reads 'searched ... and found no fine against it', a false clean on a regulatory red flag.
findings.fix: In matchCase, strip the file's own LEGAL_FORM matches from each party before calling matchOrgName. When the party starts with the company's full key (dropping 'the') followed by other words, fall back to a 'leading/padded' hit (possible, 'verify it is the same company') instead of null. Add tests for 'Klarna Bank AB', 'Avast Software s.r.o.', 'Deliveroo Italy s.r.l.' and 'Vinted UAB'.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced: matchCase returns null for 'Klarna Bank AB', 'Avast Software s.r.o.', 'Deliveroo Italy s.r.l.' and 'Vinted UAB'. exposure.js LEGAL has no sro/uab/ou/kft/doo, and 'leading' needs a LEGAL word right after descriptors. With no hits, run() writes 'found no fine against it', a false clean.
findings.betterFix: Strip gdprFines' own LEGAL_FORM words from each party before calling matchOrgName, rather than widening exposure.js LEGAL, which other matchers share. When a party starts with the full company key and then adds non-filler words, return a 'possible' hit with a 'verify it is the same company' note. Add tests for the four names and keep 'Uber B.V.' exact.

findings.title: NHTSA recalls under the maker's own legal name ('Rivian Automotive, LLC') are dropped and called another manufacturer's
findings.evidence: Live NHTSA data lists 'Rivian Automotive, LLC' (25 recalls), 'Lucid USA, Inc.' (23) and 'Fisker Group Inc' (6). With the company 'Rivian', run() returned no findings and the note 'no recall filed under that name was found'. With the legal name learned through addCompanyAlias, it returned 3 'company' findings.
findings.scenario: No legal name is learned for the company, which is typical for a private startup: Rivian, Lucid, Fisker, Canoo, Owlet, Proterra, Workhorse or Peloton Interactive. whichName/sameCompany rejects a firm that adds descriptor words, so every recall is dropped. The notes then say no recall was found and list the company's own legal entity among 'other manufacturers'. government.js byKnownName (USAspending, FDA, NIH) uses the same whichName and loses the same records.
findings.fix: When a firm's tokens start with the company's full distinctive name and only descriptor, padding or legal words follow (Automotive, USA, Group, Interactive, Technologies, Operating Company), treat it as that company's name: 'company' when the name is not an ordinary word, 'possible' otherwise. Never list such a firm under 'other manufacturers'. Add a test for 'Rivian Automotive, LLC' with company 'Rivian' and no alias.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced: whichName('Rivian Automotive, LLC',['Rivian']), 'Lucid USA, Inc.' and 'Fisker Group Inc' all return ''. companyKeyStrict keeps 'automotive', 'usa' and 'group', so sameCompany fails. The records end up in 'others', and the notes say no recall was found.
findings.betterFix: In recalls byKnownName, before the firm goes to 'others', add a fallback: the firm's strict key starts with the company's full key, and only descriptor or padding words (PADDING/SECTOR-like, plus automotive, motors, usa, group) follow. Grade that 'possible' with a verify reason, and never list the firm as another manufacturer. Leave sameCompany itself unchanged, because courts and government use it.

findings.title: 'Ended SAM.gov exclusions included' is untrue: the public search returns only active exclusions, so the fix works only on test data
findings.evidence: A live SAM sgs search for 'john smith' without is_active returned 11 rows, all isActive true, the same count as with is_active=true. With is_active=false, SAM answered 403 'Unauthorized to view inactive exclusions.' The ended-exclusion path is tested only with synthetic rows (founderR3.watchlists.test.js:377).
findings.scenario: A founder's SAM.gov debarment ran from 2016 to 2019. Dropping is_active=true does not return it, because anonymous callers cannot see inactive exclusions. The screen still reads 'SAM.gov exclusion list: no match', and the header comment and FOUNDER-CHECK coverage text imply that ended exclusions were screened. The 'exclusion ended' branch is dead code in production.
findings.fix: Correct the comments (lines 14 and 1136-1141) and add a note to every SAM screen: 'SAM.gov shows the public only exclusions in force; ended exclusions were not screened.' Keep the ended branch for the rare row whose termination date has passed but is still active. Do not claim coverage of past debarments in FOUNDER-CHECK.md.
findings.verifyNote: Live check: without is_active, all 11 rows for 'john smith' are isActive true. With is_active=false, SAM answers 403 'Unauthorized to view inactive exclusions.' The header (line 14) and the samSearch comments claim ended exclusions are included. The 'no match' note implies past debarments were screened.
findings.betterFix: Fix the comments at lines 14 and 1136-1141. Add a standing note to the SAM screen: 'SAM.gov shows the public only exclusions currently in force; ended exclusions were not screened.' Keep the ended branch for rows whose termination date has passed but which are still listed. Align the FOUNDER-CHECK.md coverage text.

findings.title: About 1,200 Denied Persons List orders that expired years ago are reported as current high-severity sanctions matches
findings.evidence: In the live CSL file, 1,207 DPL rows have an end_date in the past, some as early as 2000-2008. Screening 'Keisuke Katsuta' gave a finding with severity high, category sanctions, titled 'Name match on the US Consolidated Screening List: KATSUTA KEISUKE (DPL)'. Its quote ends 'End date: 2003-03-03'.
findings.scenario: A founder shares a name with a denial order that lapsed in 2003. The title and severity read as a current US sanctions or export-denial listing. If the given company appears in the record, the grade can rise to likely or confirmed and become a red flag. The audit's ended-wording fix was applied only to EBRD and SAM.gov, not to the screening list's own end_date column.
findings.fix: In listRecord/matchFinding, compare row.e (yyyy-mm-dd) with today. For an end date in the past, title the finding 'Formerly listed on <list> (ended <date>)', lower the severity to medium, and add data.ended, as ebrdFinding does. Add a test with a DPL row whose end date has passed.
findings.verifyNote: In screenList, severity is fixed at 'high' and the title is 'Name match on the US Consolidated Screening List'. listRecord only adds 'End date: X' to the quote. Nothing compares row.e with today, so a denial order that lapsed in 2003 reads as a current listing.
findings.betterFix: In listRecord, return an ended flag when row.e < today. In screenList, group ended records apart: use 'on the <list> (listing ended <date>)' as where, severity medium, and data.ended. Mirror the SAM over/ended pattern. Add a test with a past-dated DPL row.
